text: Money is anything that people accept as payment for goods and services. People also use it to repay debts.
Most modern textbooks list three jobs of money: a medium of exchange, a unit of account and a store of value.
The Mesopotamian shekel was a unit of weight. It relied on the mass of something like 160 grains of barley.
Barter is a way of trading in which people directly swap goods or services for other goods or services. They do not use money.
Coins are standardized in weight. They are made in large numbers at a mint to make trade easier.
Coins last longer than banknotes. Banknotes last only about four years, compared with 30 years for a coin.
A transaction is an exchange of goods or services. It can be done with money or without it.
Markets make trading easier. They let people compare and set prices for the things they trade.
A merchant is a person or company that is engaged in trade. Merchants sell through stores or online platforms.
Merchants worked in ancient Egypt, Greece, China and India. They also worked in Babylonia, Persia, Phoenicia and Rome.
The Phoenicians were well known as traders in purple. They controlled the purple dye made from the murex shell.
The Sari-i-Sang mine in the mountains of Afghanistan was the largest source for trade of lapis lazuli.
Clocks led people to divide work time into hours. That is how the idea of an hourly wage began.
Wages were paid in the Middle Kingdom of ancient Egypt, ancient Greece and ancient Rome.
Seventy-five million workers earned hourly wages in the United States in 2012. They made up 59% of employees.
Wages for most workers are set by market forces. Others are set by collective bargaining, where a labor union negotiates for the workers.
The Fair Labor Standards Act sets a minimum wage at the federal level. All states must follow it.
When each worker does a single task, a group gets more done. This is called division of labor.
A business is any activity that is done for profit.
An entrepreneur is a person who creates or invests in one or more businesses. The entrepreneur bears most of the risks and enjoys most of the rewards.
Starting a new business takes new ideas, effort and a willingness to take risks.
In almost all countries, most people are employed by businesses.
A sole proprietorship, also called a sole trader, is owned by one person. It operates for that person's benefit.
One out of twelve retail businesses in the United States is franchised. 8 million people are employed in a franchised business.
Opportunity cost shows the link between scarcity and choice. Its aim is to make sure scarce resources are used well.
Opportunity costs are not only about money. The real cost can also be lost time, pleasure, or any other benefit that you give up.
Say a person leaves work for an hour to buy $200 of office supplies. Their hourly rate is $25. The $25 they could have earned instead is an opportunity cost.
In 1803, Jean-Baptiste Say defined economics as the science of how wealth is made, shared and used.
In 1849, Thomas Carlyle called classical economics "the dismal science".
Building one aircraft costs a lot of money. But when a company builds a hundred, the cost of the 100th is much lower.
Saving is income that is not spent. It is also called deferred consumption.
In economics, interest is a payment from a borrower to a lender. It is an amount above what was borrowed, at a particular rate.
In personal finance, saving usually means keeping money safe at low risk, as in a deposit account. Investment is a lot riskier.
In the United States, a bank deposit is insured up to at least $250,000 for each person at each bank. The bank needs FDIC insurance.
A bank is a financial institution that accepts deposits from the public and makes loans.
The oldest existing retail bank is Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena. It was founded in 1472.
Supply and demand is a model that explains how prices are set in a market. It is the basis of modern economics.
A price is the amount of money that buyers are willing and able to pay for a good or service. It is also the amount that sellers are willing to accept.
The most obvious example of a price is the cost of a loan. Its cost is expressed as the percentage rate of interest.
Inflation is an increase in the average price of goods and services.
When prices rise, each dollar buys less. So inflation lowers the buying power of money.
The opposite of inflation is deflation, a drop in the general price level.
International trade is mostly trade in goods and services. There is much less trade in capital, labor or other factors of production.
Cargo ships come in many sizes, from small coastal ships to huge ocean-going carriers. Each is usually built for one kind of cargo.
Container ships carry general cargo in 20-foot or 40-foot (6.1 or 12.2 m) containers. They call at a regularly published schedule of ports.
A shipping container is a box that is strong enough to withstand shipment, storage and handling.
About seventeen million intermodal containers are in use around the world. A large share of the freight shipped over long distances travels in them.
Reusable steel boxes for use as truck-sized shipping containers first came into use around 1956.
